name: The dated, ordered steps for taking a dog, cat or ferret into the United States, the European Union or Great Britain — microchip, rabies vaccination, blood test and the waiting periods between them, quoted from the law itself
description: Getting a pet across a border is a chain of steps that only counts if it is done in the right order, and every link is a date. The microchip has to go in before the rabies vaccine or the vaccine does not count; the animal has to be old enough on the day it is vaccinated; then there is a wait before travel; and from an unlisted country there is a blood sample taken a set number of days after vaccination followed by a further wait of months. One step out of order costs three months and a plane ticket. This asset records each of those provisions as its own record, quoted verbatim from the instrument that states it — 42 CFR 71.51 for entry into the United States, Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 for the European Union, and the Defra guidance at GOV.UK for Great Britain. Answers 'what is the earliest my dog can fly?', 'does the microchip have to come before the rabies shot?', 'how long after the rabies blood test can we travel?', 'how old does a dog have to be to enter the US?', and 'when does the tapeworm treatment have to be given?'
licence: Three sources, all reusable. 42 CFR 71.51 is served by eCFR (Office of the Federal Register) and is a work of the US federal government, not subject to copyright. Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 is reproduced from EUR-Lex; reuse of European Union legislation is permitted under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU with acknowledgement of the source, and only short attributed passages are quoted here. The GOV.UK guidance states on its own pages that 'All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0'. In every case we take the fact plus a short quote that links back to the page; facts are not copyrightable (Feist, 1991).

records.provision: An anti-rabies vaccination must fulfil the following conditions
records.requirement: the pet animal was at least 12 weeks old at the date on which the vaccine was administered
records.timing: not be less than 21 days from the completion of the vaccination protocol required by the manufacturer for the primary vaccination
records.ordering: the date of administration referred to in point (c) does not precede the date of application of the transponder or tattoo
records.source_quote: An anti-rabies vaccination must fulfil the following conditions: (a) | the vaccine was administered by an authorised veterinarian; | (b) | the pet animal was at least 12 weeks old at the date on which the vaccine was administered; | (c) | the date of administration of the vaccine is indicated by an authorised veterinarian or an official veterinarian in the appropriate section of the identification document; | (d) | the date of administration referred to in point (c) does not precede the date of application of the transponder or tattoo or the date of reading of the transponder or the tattoo indicated in the appropriate section of the identification document; | (e) | the period of validity of the vaccination starts from the establishment of protective immunity, which shall not be less than 21 days from the completion of the vaccination protocol required by the manufacturer for the primary vaccination

records.applies_to: Pet animals of the species listed in Part A of Annex I
records.requirement: shall be marked by the implantation of a transponder or by a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011
records.source_quote: Marking of pet animals 1. Pet animals of the species listed in Part A of Annex I shall be marked by the implantation of a transponder or by a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011.

records.provision: Validity requirements for the rabies antibody titration test
records.requirement: must be carried out on a sample collected at least 30 days after the date of vaccination
records.timing: at least 30 days after the date of vaccination
records.ordering: on a sample collected at least 30 days after the date of vaccination
records.source_quote: Validity requirements for the rabies antibody titration test 1. | The collection of the sample of blood necessary to carry out the rabies antibody titration test must be carried out and documented by an authorised veterinarian in the appropriate section of the identification document; | 2. | The rabies antibody titration test: (a) | must be carried out on a sample collected at least 30 days after the date of vaccination and: (i) | not less than three months before the date of: — | the non-commercial movement from a territory or a third country other than those listed in the implementing acts adopted pursuant to Article 13(1) or (2), or | — | the transit through such a territory or third country, where the conditions laid down in point (c) of Article 12 are not fulfilled

records.requirement: Your pet can enter Great Britain (England, Wales and Scotland) with an animal health certificate (AHC) if all the following apply
records.timing: it’s less than 6 months since the date you entered the EU or a country that accepts AHCs
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Animal health certificate (AHC)
records.source_quote: Animal health certificate (AHC) Your pet can enter Great Britain (England, Wales and Scotland) with an animal health certificate (AHC) if all the following apply: the AHC was issued in Great Britain you’re travelling from the EU or another country where you can use an AHC it’s less than 6 months since the date you entered the EU or a country that accepts AHCs

records.provision: How to get your pet a rabies blood test
records.requirement: Your pet must have a blood sample taken at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination
records.timing: 3 months from the date the blood sample was taken
records.ordering: a blood sample taken at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Blood tests for rabies — How to get your pet a rabies blood test
records.source_quote: How to get your pet a rabies blood test Your pet must have a blood sample taken at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination. Your vet must send the blood sample to an EU-approved blood testing laboratory from either inside the EU or outside the EU . The results of the blood test must show that the vaccination was successful (rabies antibody level of at least 0.5 IU/ml). The vet must give you a copy of the test results and enter the day the blood sample was taken in a pet passport or Great Britain health certificate . You must wait 3 months from the date the blood sample was taken before you travel.

records.provision: If your dog has had the Canvac DHPPiL+ R vaccination
records.applies_to: If your dog has the Canvac DHPPiL + R vaccine
records.requirement: your dog has had 3 doses of the primary course of the vaccine
records.timing: at least 21 weeks old before they travel
records.ordering: each vaccine dose was 3 weeks apart
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Rabies vaccination and boosters — If your dog has had the Canvac DHPPiL+ R vaccination
records.source_quote: If your dog has had the Canvac DHPPiL+ R vaccination If your dog has the Canvac DHPPiL + R vaccine, both of the following must apply: your dog has had 3 doses of the primary course of the vaccine each vaccine dose was 3 weeks apart Your dog must also be at least 21 weeks old before they travel.

records.provision: If your pet has had the Canvac R vaccination
records.applies_to: If your dog, cat or ferret has had the Canvac R vaccination
records.requirement: they must have had the right number of doses of the primary course
records.timing: at least 17 weeks old before they travel
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Rabies vaccination and boosters — If your pet has had the Canvac R vaccination
records.source_quote: If your pet has had the Canvac R vaccination If your dog, cat or ferret has had the Canvac R vaccination, they must have had the right number of doses of the primary course. They’ll need: 1 dose if they were vaccinated over the age of 5 months 2 doses if they were vaccinated under the age of 5 months - the doses must have been 2 to 4 weeks apart All pets with the Canvac R vaccination must be at least 17 weeks old before they travel.

records.requirement: You must get your pet microchipped before, or at the same time as, their rabies vaccination
records.ordering: before, or at the same time as, their rabies vaccination
records.consequence: they’ll need to be vaccinated again
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Microchip
records.source_quote: Microchip You must get your pet microchipped before, or at the same time as, their rabies vaccination. If you do not, they’ll need to be vaccinated again.

records.requirement: You must get your dog, cat or ferret vaccinated against rabies before they can travel
records.ordering: vaccinated against rabies before they can travel
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Rabies vaccination and boosters
records.source_quote: Rabies vaccination and boosters You must get your dog, cat or ferret vaccinated against rabies before they can travel.

records.requirement: A vet must treat your dog for tapeworm every time you want to bring it to Great Britain (England, Wales and Scotland)
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Tapeworm treatment for dogs
records.source_quote: Tapeworm treatment for dogs A vet must treat your dog for tapeworm every time you want to bring it to Great Britain (England, Wales and Scotland).

records.provision: When to get the rabies vaccinations
records.requirement: Your vet needs proof that your pet’s at least 12 weeks old before vaccinating them
records.timing: at least 21 full days after the first rabies vaccination
records.consequence: they’ll need to be vaccinated again
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Rabies vaccination and boosters — When to get the rabies vaccinations
records.source_quote: When to get the rabies vaccinations Your vet needs proof that your pet’s at least 12 weeks old before vaccinating them. You must get your pet microchipped before, or at the same time as, their rabies vaccination. If you do not, they’ll need to be vaccinated again. Ask your vet how long you must wait before travelling - some rabies vaccinations take longer to work than others. You will have to wait at least 21 full days after the first rabies vaccination (or the last of the first course of rabies vaccinations) is given. Day 1 is the day after the rabies vaccination.

records.provision: When to give the tapeworm treatment
records.requirement: The treatment must be given: no less than 24 hours before you enter Great Britain no more than 5 days (120 hours) before you enter Great Britain
records.timing: no more than 5 days (120 hours) before you enter Great Britain
records.citation: GOV.UK, Bring your pet to Great Britain: Tapeworm treatment for dogs — When to give the tapeworm treatment
records.source_quote: When to give the tapeworm treatment The treatment must be given: no less than 24 hours before you enter Great Britain no more than 5 days (120 hours) before you enter Great Britain

records.applies_to: All dogs presented for admission into the United States
records.requirement: must be at least six (6) months old at the time of their arrival into the United States
records.consequence: shall be denied admission and returned to the country of departure
records.source_quote: Age requirement for all dogs. (1) All dogs presented for admission into the United States must be at least six (6) months old at the time of their arrival into the United States. (2) Dogs arriving into the United States that are not at least six (6) months old at the time of their arrival shall be denied admission and returned to the country of departure

records.provision: CDC dog import form for all dogs
records.requirement: must submit a complete and accurate CDC dog import form to CDC via a CDC-approved system prior to the dogs arriving in the United States
records.ordering: prior to the dogs arriving in the United States
records.source_quote: CDC dog import form for all dogs. (1) All importers of dogs must submit a complete and accurate CDC dog import form to CDC via a CDC-approved system prior to the dogs arriving in the United States. This includes accompanied or unaccompanied dogs arriving by air, land, or sea regardless of where the dogs originated or whether arriving as cargo, checked-baggage, or hand-carried baggage.

records.applies_to: All dogs presented for admission into the United States
records.requirement: must have a microchip implanted prior to arrival at the U.S. port
records.ordering: The microchip must have been implanted on or before the date the current rabies vaccine was administered
records.consequence: Rabies vaccines administered prior to the implantation of a microchip are invalid.
records.source_quote: Microchip requirements for all dogs. (1) All dogs presented for admission into the United States must have a microchip implanted prior to arrival at the U.S. port. (2) The microchip must have been implanted on or before the date the current rabies vaccine was administered. Rabies vaccines administered prior to the implantation of a microchip are invalid.

records.provision: Quarantine requirements for animals at CDC-registered animal care facilities
records.applies_to: Foreign-vaccinated dogs that have been in a DMRVV high-risk country within six months of arrival
records.requirement: must be quarantined for 28 days after revaccination with a USDA-licensed rabies vaccine at the facility if they do not have a valid rabies serologic test from a CDC-approved laboratory
records.source_quote: Quarantine requirements for animals at CDC-registered animal care facilities. (1) A CDC-registered animal care facility must maintain a quarantine area for holding animals when quarantine is required. Foreign-vaccinated dogs that have been in a DMRVV high-risk country within six months of arrival must be quarantined for 28 days after revaccination with a USDA-licensed rabies vaccine at the facility if they do not have a valid rabies serologic test from a CDC-approved laboratory.

records.provision: Requirement for Certification of U.S.-Issued Rabies Vaccination form for importers seeking to import U.S.-vaccinated dogs from DMRVV high-risk countries
records.applies_to: Importers returning to the United States with a U.S.-vaccinated dog that has been in a DMRVV high-risk country within the last six months
records.requirement: may present their dog for admission without a rabies serologic test from a CDC-approved laboratory, without the dog undergoing veterinary examination (unless ill, injured, or exposed), and without revaccination against rabies or quarantine at a CDC-registered animal care facility upon arrival
records.source_quote: Requirement for Certification of U.S.-Issued Rabies Vaccination form for importers seeking to import U.S.-vaccinated dogs from DMRVV high-risk countries. (1) Importers returning to the United States with a U.S.-vaccinated dog that has been in a DMRVV high-risk country within the last six months may present their dog for admission without a rabies serologic test from a CDC-approved laboratory, without the dog undergoing veterinary examination (unless ill, injured, or exposed), and without revaccination against rabies or quarantine at a CDC-registered animal care facility upon arrival under the following circumstances:

records.provision: Requirement for proof that a dog has been only in DMRVV low-risk or DMRVV-free countries
records.applies_to: Dogs arriving, including those returning to the United States, from a DMRVV low-risk or DMRVV-free country
records.requirement: may be admitted into the United States subject to the requirements in this section if the importer submits written documentation satisfactory to the Director that for the six months before arrival, the dog has been only in DMRVV low-risk or DMRVV-free countries
records.timing: for the six months before arrival
records.source_quote: Requirement for proof that a dog has been only in DMRVV low-risk or DMRVV-free countries. (1) Dogs arriving, including those returning to the United States, from a DMRVV low-risk or DMRVV-free country may be admitted into the United States subject to the requirements in this section if the importer submits written documentation satisfactory to the Director that for the six months before arrival, the dog has been only in DMRVV low-risk or DMRVV-free countries.

records.provision: Veterinary examination, revaccination against rabies, and quarantine at a CDC-registered animal care facility for foreign-vaccinated dogs from DMRVV high-risk countries
records.applies_to: All dogs arriving into the United States that have been in DMRVV high-risk countries within the last six months and that do not have a valid certification of U.S.-issued rabies vaccination form
records.requirement: shall undergo veterinary examination and revaccination against rabies at a CDC-registered animal care facility upon arrival
records.source_quote: Veterinary examination, revaccination against rabies, and quarantine at a CDC-registered animal care facility for foreign-vaccinated dogs from DMRVV high-risk countries. (1) All dogs arriving into the United States that have been in DMRVV high-risk countries within the last six months and that do not have a valid certification of U.S.-issued rabies vaccination form shall undergo veterinary examination and revaccination against rabies at a CDC-registered animal care facility upon arrival.
